title: Living with asthma: an action plan
what: Asthma is a condition in which the airways narrow easily. With the right treatment and an action plan, most people live a normal life.
why: For all adults with asthma and their family.
duration: the plan is made at a doctor's visit; treatment is usually ongoing
tell_doctor: How often you have attacks and wake up at night
How often you use the quick-relief inhaler
What triggers attacks: dust, animals, cold, exercise
If you smoke or people around you smoke

prepare.title: Action plan
prepare.text: Ask your doctor for a written plan: what to do every day and when you get worse.

prepare.title: Inhalers
prepare.text: Show your doctor how you take a breath from the inhaler. Mistakes in technique are a common reason for poor control.

prepare.title: Triggers
prepare.text: Find out what causes your attacks and try to avoid it.

bring: A symptom diary or a peak flow meter, if you have one
steps: Use your controller inhaler every day as your doctor prescribed
During an attack, sit up straight and breathe calmly
Take puffs of the quick-relief inhaler as in your plan
If it does not help, follow the red zone of your plan and call emergency services
Write down how many times you used the quick-relief inhaler
feel: With good control, you have few attacks or none
After the inhaler, you may have a shaky feeling or a racing heart that usually passes quickly
after: After a steroid inhaler, rinse your mouth with water
See your doctor regularly, even if you feel fine
Do not stop your daily treatment on your own when you feel better
red_flags: Severe shortness of breath, or it is hard to speak: call emergency services
The quick-relief inhaler does not help or you need it very often: call emergency services
Blue lips or fingernails: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually yes. Ask your doctor if you should take a puff before exercise.

faq.q: Are the steroids in the inhaler harmful?
faq.a: The dose in inhalers is small and works mostly on the airways. Do not stop on your own, and talk to your doctor.

reminders.text: Do not forget your daily inhaler. Keep the quick-relief one with you.
